original_question: Determine whether there exists a separable II1 factor N that admits an existential embedding of L(F2) into N but is not isomorphic to a nontrivial free product.
target_in_paper: Problem 7 in the section "Existential embeddings": the paper asks whether there exists a separable II_1 factor admitting an existential embedding of L(F_2) and which is not isomorphic to a non trivial free product.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact open problem in the paper: it uses the right source factor L(F_2), the right target object (a separable II_1 factor N), the right model-theoretic hypothesis (existential embedding), and the right structural negation (N should fail to be isomorphic to a nontrivial free product).
missing_details: The paper's notion of existential embedding is the ultrapower one: an embedding i: M -> N is existential if there exists an embedding j: N -> M^U into a tracial ultrapower such that j o i is the diagonal embedding of M.
To be fully stand-alone, the ambient category should be stated explicitly: these are tracial von Neumann algebras/II_1 factors, and the free product is the tracial free product in that category.
In this operator-algebraic context, "separable" means separable predual; the draft leaves that standard convention implicit.

The phrase "nontrivial free product" is left informal in the paper; a stand-alone rewrite should spell it out as excluding the trivial scalar case, e.g. N is not isomorphic to P * Q with both P and Q non-scalar tracial von Neumann algebras.
refined_question: Does there exist a separable II_1 factor N and an existential embedding i: L(F_2) -> N, in the sense that for some nonprincipal ultrafilter U on N there is an embedding j: N -> L(F_2)^U such that j o i is the diagonal embedding of L(F_2), with the property that N is not isomorphic, as a tracial von Neumann algebra, to any nontrivial tracial free product P * Q (that is, with both P and Q non-scalar)?
justification: This draft is essentially a direct restatement of Problem 7, and the distinctive phrase "not isomorphic to a non trivial free product" singles it out from nearby existential-embedding questions such as Problem 8 (Cartan subalgebras) and Problem 10 (primeness). The only paper-faithful details that were still implicit are the ultrapower definition of existential embedding supplied immediately before Problem 7, the ambient tracial von Neumann algebra setting, and the conventional meaning of "separable" and "nontrivial free product." The annotation immediately after Problem 7 also confirms that this exact problem, rather than a broader neighboring one, is the intended target by mentioning mild negative evidence coming from free complementation results.
